A_general.open_code_note: The official repository is a local stdio MCP package using WEBFLOW_TOKEN and a Designer bridge. Its README describes remote installation separately; the source's local handlers are not identified as the implementation deployed at the input /mcp endpoint. The hosted endpoint's tool inventory is therefore taken from current hosted-server documentation.
A_general.implementation_language: Hosted endpoint: NOT FOUND. Official local repository: TypeScript/Node.js.
A_general.mcp_sdk_and_version: Hosted endpoint: NOT FOUND. Official local repository: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.25.2.
A_general.release_status: The official MCP 2.0 announcement says available to all users; Campaigns is marked Early Access. No separate formal release-status label found for the endpoint.
other_official_servers: https://mcp.webflow.com/beta/mcp — Webflow Beta MCP server for in-development functionality.

https://developers.webflow.com/_mcp/server — developer-documentation MCP server for querying Webflow documentation; separate from the product endpoint. A legacy/other documentation endpoint in the evidence set is https://developers.webflow.com/api/fern-docs/mcp.
The public GitHub package is a separate local stdio MCP implementation, not the input hosted endpoint.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: Webflow states MCP is available on all Site plans, including free Starter, and the MCP 2.0 announcement says it is available at no additional cost. Some exposed product features require paid add-ons or higher-tier plans.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Official pricing lists Starter as free, Basic at USD 15/month billed yearly, and Premium at USD 25/month billed yearly. Team is listed at USD 2,500/month with an annual contract; Enterprise is custom-priced. Prices are per site where stated, before taxes.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: MCP use itself has no additional Webflow charge and does not use Webflow AI credits; usage may count against the AI client's own plan or credits. Analyze, Optimize, and AEO tools require their corresponding add-ons on paid Site plans. Webflow Cloud has separate usage limits and charges.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: OAuth authorization is workspace-scoped; the user chooses the site/workspace access, and current Help Center guidance says users with any site role except Reviewer can connect. Access still follows product roles and permissions. Branches require Enterprise; Campaigns requires Early Access. Some canvas tools require an open Designer and connected Bridge App.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Webflow controls endpoint and product-plan feature availability; workspace/site administrators control user roles and access; the user selects sites/workspace during OAuth; the AI client controls its own usage limits.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: The hosted documentation lists 37 named tool groups: 30 data tools, 3 Designer-session tools, and 4 utility tools. Their tables enumerate 309 action variants. Data and utility tools are headless; canvas-dependent Designer tools require the Bridge App.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Documentation describes structured tool results and ModeForbidden errors for unavailable Designer modes; exact endpoint error schemas are not published in the reviewed sources.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: Webflow says the server exposes read-only MCP resources, including the Webflow Guide, which supported clients can reference into agent context.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Read-only content loaded directly into client context; exact resource URI and payload were not found.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: The hosted documentation describes a prompt library for users, but does not establish that the product endpoint implements MCP prompt-list/get methods. The public local repository README says that its implementation does not include MCP prompts; that package is a distinct server variant.

Webflow states that MCP changes are recorded in the site's activity log with agent attribution and that the log can be queried through MCP. This describes product activity logging, not transport or prompt logging.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Site activity records identify MCP changes; exact record schema and retention were not found.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Hosted docs label tools/actions read, write, or both; formal MCP tool annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint) are not published. 2. No general server-enforced confirmation flow documented. A subset of data_apps_tool actions accepts dry_run; separately installed skills can preview and ask for confirmation, which is a client-side workflow. 3. OAuth metadata supports bearer header, DCR, authorization_code and refresh_token, PKCE plain/S256, and basic/post/none token auth; scopes_supported and token lifetime absent. Docs say access follows product roles, including custom roles, and one authorization is workspace-scoped. 4. No documented toolset/read-only/query-free URL mode. Beta endpoint is separate. Designer-only tools require the Bridge App and active Designer; branches require Enterprise; Campaigns requires Early Access. 5. data_apps_tool omits secret environment-variable values but returns non-secret values in plaintext; build/runtime logs are unsanitized and may contain secrets or presigned URLs. No general PII masking statement found. 6. Limits are action-specific: e.g. asset compression is rate-limited to 10 calls/minute/site; several operations have bulk caps and pagination. No general MCP quota or per-call price documented. 7. Official tool docs publish required parameter names, but not complete JSON schemas/types on these pages. Server-side validation/correction and unknown-argument behavior are not documented. 8. Webflow says MCP changes appear in site activity logs with AI attribution; MCP request/prompt telemetry and opt-out were not found. 9. No feedback/rating/survey action found in the documented hosted tool groups. ask_webflow_ai is a Webflow API help tool; the guide recommends workflow guidance. No upsell result behavior documented. 10. Site Agent Instructions are automatically supplied and may guide agents; separate skills are installed in the client. Skills, not the endpoint, can implement validation, previews, and confirmation. 11. Docs describe current site content/instructions resolving server-side; no evidence that past agent behavior changes later outputs or tool availability. 12. The input endpoint presents a flat documented tool-group set. A companion Designer Bridge App supplies live canvas context; separate beta and documentation-search servers exist. 13. No raw arbitrary API request, SQL, or script-execution escape-hatch tool appears in the complete documented list. The local repository is a different implementation; its local-code behavior is described in notes.

These name 30 data, 3 Designer, and 4 utility tool groups; their tables contain 309 named action variants. No official overall total is stated. All 37 official group names are in actions.json; required parameter names are included per variant, but types are not published on these reference pages. No catalogue-only tool names were added. Claude's third-party connector page says “Show all 34 tools” but visibly lists 24 names; those listed names are a subset of official names. MartechDB and Agent Discoverability each report 34 tools. mcp.so has no tool list available. The 34-versus-37 difference is recorded under contradictions.

E_aggregated.token_method: The public repository is a distinct local server variant. Hosted documentation does not provide the complete serialized hosted tool schemas and initialize instructions needed for the specified character-count estimate.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: Documented limits include creating new website projects, creating localized CMS items, controlling all element settings and all CMS binding settings, managing remotely hosted Google/Adobe Fonts, editing Classic interactions, and completing the Campaigns steps for connecting marketing forms or pushing assets to ad platforms. A few visual-context actions (snapshot, selection, canvas/page/mode/branch state) need the open Designer and Bridge App. Source: https://developers.webflow.com/mcp/reference/overview and https://developers.webflow.com/mcp/tools/data-tools.md.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The utility-tool page tells agents to pull recommended workflow guidance before tasks and to use get_more_tools when available tools seem insufficient. Site Agent Instructions guide agent behavior; skills can validate, preview, and request confirmation. These are documented as guidance/client workflows; no general server enforcement is stated.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Webflow says it enforces existing roles, including custom roles, and records agent changes in site activity logs. The data_apps_tool page says secret environment variable values are omitted, while warning that build/runtime logs are unsanitized and may contain secrets or presigned URLs. AI Terms state: “Webflow will not (and will not permit its subcontractors to) use them to train, improve, or fine-tune the AI Offerings or any underlying models without Customer’s prior consent.” The reviewed terms do not specifically establish whether all MCP prompts/results fall within that defined AI Offering scope.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Webflow describes the MCP 2.0 service as available at no additional cost and says agents work with existing Webflow permissions. Its overview says agents can make site changes and that site activity logs record them.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Role enforcement and site activity logging are stated as server/product behavior, but implementation details are not public for the hosted endpoint. Secret omission is documented for data_apps_tool; unsanitized logs are an explicit limitation. Guidance and skill confirmation are not general endpoint-level enforcement. AI Terms make a no-training commitment for covered AI Offerings; MCP-specific applicability is not explicit in the reviewed policy. No endpoint-specific retention or MCP telemetry opt-out statement found.

contradictions: The current official tool reference documents 37 tool groups (30 data, 3 Designer, 4 utility), while the Claude connector directory says “Show all 34 tools” and lists 24; MartechDB and Agent Discoverability report 34. The catalogue names shown are a subset of official names, and no extra catalogue-only tools were added.

The Webflow Help Center overview says Analyze support is site-level only and that page-level analysis, goal reporting, and filtered queries are unavailable. Current official MCP documentation lists page-flow, goal, and query-oriented Analyze actions, including get_goal_performance and get_page_flow_report. The docs appear out of sync.

The official local repository README says that its implementation does not include MCP prompts or resources, while current hosted-server documentation says the hosted server exposes resources. The repository is a distinct local server variant, so this is a variant difference rather than evidence about the hosted endpoint.
observations_for_research: Tool-level permission grants every action within a grouped tool, rather than a separately configurable permission for each listed action.
The documented action inventory has grown and changed across MCP versions; Webflow publishes a migration guide mapping older tool/action names to current names.
The hosted system combines a remote headless API surface with a live Designer bridge for a subset of visual-context operations.
notes: Checked links.json, pages/ and local repository copies first. The official endpoint returned 401 as supplied; its own protected-resource metadata was used without re-fetching. The repo is official but is a local stdio implementation, not identified as the hosted /mcp server; local code confirms WEBFLOW_TOKEN auth, MCP instructions, a User-Agent header, and separate designer bridge handlers. Help Center URLs were captured as HTTP 403 in the evidence folder, so their content was cross-checked through official web search. Reviewed official docs, pricing, AI Terms, privacy policy, Claude connector directory, MartechDB, Agent Discoverability and mcp.so. Composio's captured toolkit page concerns its general Webflow toolkit, not confirmed tools for this endpoint, and is not used as action evidence.
